scene_text: INT. BATHROOM - NIGHT. A cramped bathroom set, 4 by 3.5 metres. A sink and mirror cabinet on the back wall, a bathtub along the right wall with its curtain drawn. NORA (40s) washes her face at the sink, eyes closed. She looks up into the mirror: nothing. She opens the cabinet, closes it — and in the mirror a pale woman now stands behind her, by the bathtub. Nora spins around. Nobody there. Slow Dutch drift during the washing, a mirror reveal, and a fast turn-around reveal of the empty bathtub.

scene.title: It Was Never There
scene.logline: A woman washing her face at a bathroom sink sees a pale apparition appear in the mirror behind her, but when she turns, the room is empty — until the cabinet closes one last time.
scene.mood: quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt

beats.description: Nora leans over the sink, eyes shut, water running; slow Dutch drift begins and the mirror cabinet hangs dark above her.
She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own face and the empty room behind her.
She opens the cabinet, blocking the mirror; when it clicks shut, the pale woman is standing by the bathtub in the reflection.
Nora spins around to face the bathtub — nobody there, just the drawn curtain and the empty mat.
She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet door swings open on its own and the pale woman is now directly behind her reflection, close enough to touch.

references.moment: Danny leans over the bathroom sink; camera tracks down the hall and into the mirror.
references.technique: Slow Steadicam track-in toward a mirror.
references.why: This is the exact grammar of your opening — a slow, patient drift toward a figure hunched over a sink whose reflection is the real subject, letting the mirror itself become the destination of the move (serves t=0s).

references.moment: Carol shuts the closet door; a man's reflection is suddenly visible in the mirror.
references.why: The camera never moves and never shows the intruder directly — the horror exists purely inside the mirror, which is precisely how the pale woman should arrive at t=9s when the cabinet clicks shut.

references.moment: Opening 360-degree single-take pan circling a suburban street.
references.why: A full rotation that returns to where it started and finds nothing is the cleanest cinematic expression of Nora spinning to face the bathtub and finding only a curtain — the pan itself does the "it was never there" work (serves t=12s).

references.moment: Peter moves through the dark house; the slow camera gradually reveals Annie on the ceiling.
references.technique: Slow patient reveal within deep, dark space.
references.why: The threat is already in frame before the audience registers it — the ideal model for t=14s, where the pale woman is standing behind Nora's reflection and the camera simply lets you find her a beat too late.

techniques.name: Mirror reveal
techniques.effect: the jump scare is behind the character, seen in a reflection
techniques.move: Frame the character in a mirror; push gently or rack focus as a figure appears behind them.
techniques.rig_notes: Keep the camera out of the mirror's reflection line: angle 20-30 degrees off the mirror normal.
techniques.matched_beat: She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet door swings open on its own and the pale woman is now directly behind her reflection, close enough to touch. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

techniques.name: Pull-back isolation
techniques.effect: loneliness; the character becomes small and vulnerable
techniques.move: Start on a medium close-up, pull straight back and up slightly to a wide.
techniques.rig_notes: Back along the rail axis; watch reach when the camera rises at the far end.
techniques.matched_beat: She straightens and looks into the mirror: only her own face and the empty room behind her. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

techniques.name: Dutch angle drift
techniques.effect: unease, something is wrong with the world
techniques.move: Slow roll from level to 10-25 degrees while drifting sideways.
techniques.rig_notes: Roll is wrist 3; cheap for the arm.
techniques.examples: The Third Man; The Exorcist III
techniques.matched_beat: Nora leans over the sink, eyes shut, water running; slow Dutch drift begins and the mirror cabinet hangs dark above her. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

techniques.name: Slow lateral reveal
techniques.effect: suspense; the audience scans the frame for what is hidden
techniques.move: Track sideways past a doorway, pillar or furniture so a figure is revealed in the background.
techniques.rig_notes: The ideal rail move: mostly the carriage axis, joints almost static.
techniques.examples: Hereditary attic; The Conjuring clapping game
techniques.matched_beat: She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet door swings open on its own and the pale woman is now directly behind her reflection, close enough to touch. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

techniques.name: Peek around the corner
techniques.effect: the camera itself behaves like an intruder
techniques.move: Camera starts hidden behind a wall or doorframe and slowly leans out to reveal the room.
techniques.rig_notes: Small lateral move plus a slight yaw. Do not intersect the wall prop.
techniques.matched_beat: She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet door swings open on its own and the pale woman is now directly behind her reflection, close enough to touch. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

techniques.name: Whip pan reveal
techniques.effect: jolt; the audience's attention is snatched to a threat
techniques.move: Hold on subject, then a fast pan of 60-120 degrees to the threat in 0.4-0.8 s, settle on it.
techniques.rig_notes: Hard for heavy arms: wrist and base joints spike. Ease in for a few tenths of a second and keep the camera position nearly still.
techniques.matched_beat: She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet door swings open on its own and the pale woman is now directly behind her reflection, close enough to touch. (quiet routine curdling into a mirror jolt)

shot_list.director_notes: We shoot the bathroom as a patient, almost boring space so the mirror can betray it. The rail sits at y=2.1, giving the arm a clean 0.8 m standoff from Nora's mark at y=2.9 and keeping the whole rig out of the mirror's reflection line; every camera position stays at least 0.8 m from both actor marks and clear of the sink, tub and curtain boxes. The first two shots are slow and lateral, the third is a controlled 360° pan that ends on nothing, and the last is a static mirror frame where the pale woman is already in the glass a beat before we cut.

shots.name: Sink Drift
shots.intent: Establish quiet routine and let a slow roll make the audience uneasy before anything happens; the mirror cabinet hangs dark at the top of frame like a held breath.
shots.reference_title: The Shining (1980) — Danny leans over the bathroom sink; camera tracks down the hall and into the mirror

shots.name: Mirror Reveal
shots.intent: Nora straightens and looks into the mirror; the camera pushes gently and racks focus so the audience scans the empty room behind her and finds nothing — priming them to look again at t=9.
shots.reference_title: Repulsion (1965) — Carol shuts the closet door; a man's reflection is suddenly visible in the mirror

shots.name: Nothing There
shots.intent: Nora spins to face the bathtub and the camera pans with her in one unbroken rotation that returns to the mirror and finds only the curtain and the empty mat — the move itself performs the 'it was never there' beat.
shots.reference_title: It Follows (2014) — Opening 360-degree single-take pan circling a suburban street

shots.name: Behind the Reflection
shots.intent: She turns back to the mirror; the cabinet swings open on its own and the pale woman is already standing behind Nora's reflection, close enough to touch — the camera holds still and lets the audience find her a beat too late.
shots.reference_title: Hereditary (2018) — Peter moves through the dark house; the slow camera gradually reveals Annie on the ceiling

notes: Listen up. The scare is the classic false relief: she spins, finds nothing, turns back — and the cabinet's open with the pale woman already behind her reflection. Four shots, escalating rhythm: slow Dutch drift on the sink, gentle push and rack focus into the mirror, one unbroken 360 that comes back empty, then hold dead still and let them find her a beat too late. No cuts on S3 — it's one move, rehearse it. Safety: the cabinet swings on a motor, so clear the counter and keep Nora's hands off the mirror rig.
